clinician.trajectory_summary: A 79-year-old female with 18-year history of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c 17.85%) presented with acute onset right-sided dance-like involuntary movements (chorea) lasting 1 day, aggravated during wakefulness and absent during sleep, accompanied by decreased muscle tension in the right limbs. Admission laboratory studies revealed severe hyperglycemia (random glucose 33.3 mmol/L) without ketosis (urinary ketone negative). Computed tomography excluded structural lesions (cerebral infarction, hemorrhage, or tumor) in the basal ganglia. Brain MRI demonstrated metabolic striatal abnormalities with low ADC signals and high E-ADC signals in the left basal ganglia contralateral to the chorea. Alternative etiologies were excluded by normal EEG, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, copper studies, ceruloplasmin, iron, ferritin, and antinuclear antibodies. The patient was treated with intravenous insulin for glycemic control and haloperidol (5 mg intramuscular daily for 3 days, followed by oral 2 mg twice daily). The chorea gradually decreased after 3 days and completely resolved after 7 days of treatment.
